keyframes.prompt:
Use case: identity-preserve. Asset: 2D game animation key-pose sheet for Shion. Reference image 1 is the exact visual identity source and image 2 is a padded version of the same baseline. Generate ONE transparent PNG sheet, exactly FOUR equal square cells in a 2 by 2 grid, reading order anticipation/contact/follow-through/recovery. Prefer 2048x2048 total resolution, cells 1024 square. Entire character and sword inside each cell, broad empty transparent gutters. No text, numbers, labels, grid lines, ground, shadow, motion trails, particles or scenery. Draw the complete character fresh in each pose, not cutout limb rotation. Preserve precisely the reference's rose-pink loose long hair, teal eyes, black hair clip, face, mature natural proportions, white cropped military jacket/gold epaulets, black cropped top, black tactical shorts, long black gloves, black boots, plum waist half-cape, forearm command gauntlet, and ONE long black/silver mechanical greatsword with chamber guard and split cyan-white core. Do not simplify the sword, change outfit or hairstyle, enlarge breasts, change shading style or make chibi. Face and fixed three-quarter camera always look screen-right. The primary sword arm remains connected to the original screen-left shoulder, support gauntlet arm to original screen-right shoulder. Same primary and support hands on the long grip throughout attack, never swap arms or hands, one sword only. Same head size, torso and limb lengths, boot positions and same grounded foot line in all four cells; body head-to-sole height approx 470 pixels in each 1024 cell, character root near cell x512, boot ground y850, leaving full room for the long sword. Pose changes may compress knees but may not resize the anatomy. Pose A / final frame02: slight knee compression, both hands raise blade up/back behind screen-left shoulder, blade points upper-left; hips rotate back, front faces right, boots planted at original positions. Pose B / frame05 contact: a decisive single downward diagonal slash toward screen-right, hips/shoulders lead hands, blade points forward-right/down about25 degrees, front knee bears weight, clearest extended contact silhouette. Pose C / frame08 follow-through: same slash arc continues a bit lower, blade forward-right/down about45 degrees, slightly lower torso, hands keep grip, hair/cape lag back. NO reverse slash or overhead reset. Pose D / frame11 recovery: torso re-centers, blade comes down-left to the baseline low guard, support gauntlet hand starting to release, near original neutral pose. Four poses must be stages of ONE continuous heavy cut. Keep all source-specific clothing and weapon details consistent across the shared sheet.
LAYOUT CORRECTION is critical: the second reference is an unacceptable crowded draft, use its pose sequence ONLY. Make every figure at least 30 percent smaller relative to its equal cell than in that draft. Each figure crown-to-boot must occupy at most 52 percent of its cell height. Every silhouette including sword must have at least 12 percent of cell width clear space on ALL sides. Sword tips may NOT approach outer sheet edges or internal grid lines. For the 2x2 grid: body root at local50%x, boots local78%y; head aroundlocal27%y. Keep complete long greatsword in every cell WITHOUT shortening sword. Exact 4 separate poses, generous empty gutters. Do not crop ANY part. Do not produce the red/cyan pixel noise seen around draft edges: clean transparent RGBA anti-aliased boundaries. Preserve design.
